chunks: From him, from Salih, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Mihran, from Abdul Malik ibn Bashir, from Usaym ibn Sulayman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When one of you wishes for the Qa'im, let him wish for him in 'afiyah (protection/wholeness), for Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a mercy, and He will send the Qa'im as a wrath.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi
key_terms.عَافِيَةٍ: Afiyah, meaning protection, safety, or wholeness from harm
key_terms.نَقِمَةً: Naqimah, meaning wrath or vengeance against enemies

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's mission as a mercy and the Qa'im's mission as a wrath?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the dual nature of the Qa'im's mission by contrasting the Prophet Muhammad's role as a mercy (rahmah) with the Awaited Imam's role as a divine wrath (naqimah) against the disbelievers. Scholars interpret 'afiyah' (well-being/safety) as the state of believers who are preserved from this wrath, emphasizing that the Qa'im's arrival brings both retribution for enemies and ultimate security for the faithful. This distinction underscores the eschatological transition from prophetic guidance to imamic enforcement of divine justice.

en.hubeali: H 14754 – From him, from Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Mahraan, from Abdul Malik Bin Basheer, from Usaym Bin Suleyman, from Muawiya Bin Ammaar, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:

‘If one of you wishes for Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> should do so with regards to ‘عَافِيَةٍ’ protection (for everyone), for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> as a mercy and Sent Al-Qaim as a Wrath’.
en.sarwar: 306. From him, from Salih, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Mahraan, from Abdul Malik Bin Basheer, from Usaym Bin Suleyman, from Muawiya Bin Ammaar, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said:
‘If one of you wishes for Al-Qaim (a.s.) should do so with regards to ‘عَافِيَةٍ’ protection (for everyone), for Allah (azwj) Sent Muhammad (saww) as a mercy and Sent Al-Qaim as a Wrath’.
